A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DynamicFace, with matching core methods and experiments. All supplied pages, equations, tables and figures support comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains readable supplementary Appendices A–C.

before.justification: v1 reports original FF++ quantitative evaluations, FF++ and FFHQ qualitative comparisons, and condition, motion-module and identity-module ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds FusionTVO evaluation, quantitative facial-condition ablations and supplementary portrait-enhancement and artifact-restoration examples.

M1.justification: Section 3.5 introduces FusionTVO, which combines position-weighted fusion of overlapping video-segment latents with temporal regularization during reverse diffusion, without retraining. This substantially extends inference beyond v1's temporal-attention module. The four facial conditions, Face Former, ReferenceNet and main training objectives remain.

E1.justification: Existing VGGFace2, VFHQ, private-data training and FF++/FFHQ swapping coverage remain. Appendix B adds qualitative tests of identity enhancement for generated portraits and motion-consistent artifact restoration in generated videos, substantially extending the evaluated task and input coverage beyond face swapping.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Deepfakes, FaceShifter, MegaFS, SimSwap, DiffSwap and Face Adapter. Supplementary Figure 7 newly compares InstantID-generated portraits with their DynamicFace-enhanced versions; InstantID appeared only in related-work discussion in v1.

E3.justification: The main training schedules, image resolution and image/video sampling procedures remain unchanged. v2 adds aesthetic scoring to Table 2 and an explicitly public, FF++-only training protocol for the additional condition ablations in Appendix A. The aesthetic scorer and supplementary ablation splits are unspecified.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds quantitative removal tests for all four facial conditions, extending v1's qualitative condition ablation, which remains as v2 Figure 5. Table 2 adds a FusionTVO ablation. Supplementary figures also provide new condition-removal examples, artifact-restoration case studies and varied-pose/illumination visualizations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 3 and the existing Table 2 metrics are unchanged. Table 2 adds FusionTVO results: consistency 99.04 and warping error 0.045, versus 99.02 and 0.046 for motion-only, plus aesthetic scores for all configurations. Table 4 and supplementary figures add substantial new condition-ablation and application outcomes.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 are retained. v2 adds a latent denoising-plus-temporal-regularization objective in Equation 8 and fusion/update expressions in Algorithm 1, invoking half-quadratic splitting. This is a limited mathematical extension without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 replaces the contribution bullet highlighting ReferenceNet/Face Former and identity consistency without identity loss with FusionTVO, claimed to eliminate segment flicker. The conclusion also credits FusionTVO for consistent video swapping. This adds a substantive central contribution; image support itself was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: Section 3.5 newly identifies residual flicker despite facial conditions and temporal attention, explaining how segment fusion and temporal regularization address it. Appendix B extends the interpretation of disentanglement to localized geometry repair and artifact correction while preserving motion and other attributes.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds inference pseudocode and identifies overlap, fusion and regularization parameters, but supplies no numerical parameter values. v1's explicit irregular-cutout augmentation disclosure disappears, without establishing that augmentation stopped. Main training/hardware details and the promised project-page access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Geman and Yang's half-quadratic regularization, FullDiT2, and Mi et al.'s 3DMM-guided face-data synthesis. Existing comparisons with face-swapping and identity-preserving research remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title and author order, adopts numbered sections and citations, and rewrites selected passages, especially ReferenceNet's description. It adds Section 3.5 and supplementary sections, while retaining the main narrative order and much of the original prose.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the visual presentation: the video teaser moves to the first page and gains examples, the overview diagram is revised, and existing illustrations are reordered. Table 2 gains a configuration and aesthetic column; Algorithm 1, Table 4 and six supplementary figures introduce substantial new displays.

improvement.justification: The public-data quantitative condition ablations strengthen support that was previously qualitative, while FusionTVO receives an explicit procedure and comparative evaluation. These are useful gains, but Table 2's incremental benefits lack uncertainty estimates, aesthetic scoring and optimizer parameter values are unspecified, and the cutout-augmentation disclosure is lost. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
